exposure: Type of stroke (Ischemic vs. Intracranial Hemorrhage)
cohort: Thirty-four Japanese women admitted to a single perinatology center between 1982 and 2012 with a diagnosis of acute cerebral stroke during pregnancy or within 6 weeks postpartum, who had no prior history of stroke or cerebrovascular abnormalities.
finding: Hemorrhagic stroke was found to be a more common etiology than ischemic stroke in this cohort, and was associated with worse maternal and fetal outcomes, including lower fetal survival, poorer maternal consciousness, and greater neurological dependency in the chronic stage.
